clues.title: Landscape: Grassy Rolling Hills
text: Grassy green rolling hills can be found in southern Kazakhstan. They are especially common just north of Bishkek

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Uzbek Border
text: The landscape in southern Kazakhstan near Uzbekistan is hilly and quite dry and shrubby, with a lot of orange looking grass. The landscape consists of dry but grassy rolling hills or dead flat agricultural land near Zhetisay.
NOTE: These red and white KM markers that look like Kyrgyz ones, are only found near Zhetisay.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Autumn Hills
text: The East Kazakhstan Region is hilly and forested. It was covered in october, so you will see fall colours on the vegetation. The town of Ridder itself is flat, but surrounded by hazy mountains.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Birch Forests
text: These lush birch forests next to green fields are common in northern Kazakhstan.
NOTE: This landscape often appears very similar to that found in and around Omsk Oblast in Russia.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Green Plains
text: Vast grassy green plains are found in northwestern Kazakhstan. They are especially common in Akmola and Kostanay regions.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Tall Mountains
text: Tall mountains, which are often snow-capped, can be seen in southeastern Kazakhstan.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Desert Landscape
text: Sandy and shrubby desert-like landscapes are common in southwestern Kazakhstan.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pedestrian sign: Pedestrian Crossing
text: Like Russia, Kazakhstan uses yellow and white stripes on their pedestrian crossings.
However, unlike Russia the stripes often have white dashes on either side.
Sometimes, you can find the dashes without the stripes.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Bollards
text: Kazakhstan uses a variety of post-Soviet style bollards, as well as ones that resemble Turkish bollards.
Notably, the bollards seemingly consisting of two thin bollards attached at a 90° angle are unique to Kazakhstan.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Car
text: All of the coverage in Kazakhstan was taken with a white pickup truck, which can either be fully visible or mostly blurred.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape
text: Kazakhstan is a big and diverse country, which features a plethora of distinct landscapes like deserts, grassy steppes, mountain passes, and birch forests.
Most strikingly, most of the rural coverage in Kazakhstan is in a very empty, open and mostly flat landscape.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pedestrian sign: Russian Infrastructure
text: A lot of Kazakh infrastructure, from pedestrian signs, poles, houses, to bollards, is very similar to what you see in Russia.
